draft.headline: Big Tech earnings pulled NQ down 2.05% on the week despite falling yields
draft.summary: NQ fell 2.05% for the week. Two up days gave way to three down days after Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon reported. Yields fell, which usually helps tech, but earnings worries appear to have mattered more.
draft.what_it_means: The week turned on Big Tech earnings. After Microsoft and Alphabet reported Wednesday, NQ was down −0.62% and −0.66% within 21 minutes. The drop grew to −1.56% by the close. Microsoft's headline said it beat on cloud growth, yet futures still slipped. Alphabet's headline flagged worry about AI spending. Amazon's miss on Thursday got little first reaction, but NQ then fell −2.45% by the close. The facts can't separate each company's effect. Elsewhere, Q3 GDP came in above forecast at 3.4%.
draft.market_reaction: NQ rose Monday (+1.12%) and Tuesday (+1.66%). It then fell Wednesday (−1.20%), Thursday (−2.10%, the biggest move) and Friday (−1.50%). Monday's jump had no clear cause in the headlines. Friday ended with a late bounce of +0.93% in about an hour. S&P 500 futures fell only 0.61% for the week, so tech led the losses. The VIX ended at 19.42, up 12.91% today. Gold fell 2.98% for the week.
draft.rates_read: Yields fell over the week. The 2-year dropped 11.3bp to 4.590%, and the 10-year dropped 9.1bp to 4.929% (bp means basis points, hundredths of a percent). Falling yields usually help Nasdaq stocks, because future tech profits are worth more today. This week NQ fell anyway. That suggests earnings and AI-spending worries outweighed rates. The Fed's target stayed at 3.75–4.00%.

draft.learn: A 'beat' can still disappoint. Microsoft's headline said it beat, yet NQ slipped. Markets judge results against hopes, and also against forward signals like spending plans. If a company beats but doesn't ease worries about costly AI spending, its stock and the index can still fall.
